rationale: mapFlat is showing at 15 iterations, so the rung is 4b by name and a season or an evening does not clear it. The watch already forbids re-deriving the map-is-full argument a fourth time and names the two honest moves that remain: a new TILE or SPECIES constant, or DEPTH beyond the grid. I SHOT THE TOWN BEFORE PLANNING IT (day 6 12.98h midsummer, day 9 19.09h late summer, wide + mobile + a crop of the near band) and the picture named the move without my having to choose it. The bottom ~15% of every wide frame is our own block, the nearest quarter, at the largest pixels in the picture — and it is 1095 cells of ONE tile, 45% of all the WALL in the town, broken only by the river slot and two light wells. Everything needed to make it a place was built years of iterations ago and never used by anything human: roofWalkZ reads the pitch bilinearly for a walker, nearScale ramps a figure to NEAR_SZ 1.95, ROOF_FURN stands 24 washing lines, tanks and lofts on rows 86-87 (the source's own note says row 87 is the one line dead level across the whole block), LOFTS are landing boards, wellNear keeps a line off a hole, and the cat already crosses it. Twenty-four objects a tenant would own, and in 169 iterations no tenant. That is a spatial 4b (a new tile, +9 in the summed census, GLASS #116 and REED #155 the precedents), it is the domain 7 back, and it is the one change that alters what a visitor sees in the first ten seconds — because it happens closer to them than anything else in the town. Every other brief in this queue carries the number it rests on and where the number came from, per the standing watch note aimed at this seat; two of them (b172, b173) carry premises I have NOT re-measured myself and say so, with the measurement named as the deliverable if they do not reproduce.

queue.brief: Our own block — rows 79..87, the bottom ~15% of every wide shot, the nearest thing in the picture — is 1095 cells of one tile. buildGrid's last branch is `wellAt(x,y) ? VOID : WALL`, so the block is WALL end to end (2441 WALL cells in the whole town; ours is 45% of them) apart from the river slot and 12 VOID cells in two light wells. Everything a roof needs to be a PLACE is already built and nothing human uses it: `roofWalkZ()` reads the pitch bilinearly for a walker, `nearScale(y)` ramps a figure to NEAR_SZ 1.95 — nearly twice the size of anyone across the lane — `ROOF_FURN` stands 24 washing lines, water tanks and pigeon lofts on rows 86-87, `LOFTS` are landing boards, `wellNear(x)` keeps a line off a hole, and `catA` already crosses on `catLine`. Twenty-four things a tenant would own, and in 169 iterations no person has ever stood among them. GIVE THE BLOCK A TOP. Cut a new tile (call it LEADS) — flat lead roof-terrace — into rows 86..87 of some of the bays, sited where the pitch is ALREADY level so no volume changes: the source's own measurement is row 87 dead level across the whole block, row 86 level to within 0.31 of a cell, against z 1.98/1.55 out on the open pitch at rows 84/85. It is WALL to `buildVolumes()` and takes its own fill in the ground cache — GLASS (line ~283) is the exact precedent for a tile with its own volume rule — and it joins `developed` in `__census()` so nothing collapses. Then put a TENANT on it, with their own source and their own cap: up out of a loft hatch to hang the washing, out to take it in when `raining` or `isWindy()` says so, out to stand at the parapet in the evening. A 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. This is the bet.
queue.successLooksLike: On a fine afternoon a figure stands on our own roof at the bottom of the wide shot, twice the size of anyone in the town, and when the rain comes on they come out and take the washing in. CENSUS OBLIGATION: `tileKinds` 153 -> 162 (a new kind is +9 in the summed 3x3 matrix) and `structures` up by the hatches; `developed` stays at 71730 because LEADS is built ground, and no other scalar collapses. Re-pin with `census.mjs --save-baseline` and SAY SO in the ledger.

RE-COUNT THE 28 ON HEAD FIRST; it is dated #154 and #159 has landed since. Then raise the SUPPLY — `allotRate` / `spawnAllotAgent`, the arrival rate and the window — never the share, and measure presence per PLOT rather than choices. Carry c257 with it, because it is the same domain and three lines: `cartToday()` and `drayToday()` are `hash(day,k)` UNSALTED, so the allotment cart's calendar is identical in every world; `WIND_SALT` exists for exactly this. Cross street x Scale/World is an EMPTY cell — 0 entries in 169 iterations.

If that reproduces, the plaza's emptiness is no longer the places but the FAMILY CAP and the band's own arrival rate. But the law says a cap and a share are two bounds and only one can be swept, and #148 already found FAM_CAP a DEAD constant past 4 — so sweep it paired per seed (`probes/town-caps.mjs`) and measure the share at the CHOICE (`probes/plaza-door.mjs`) BEFORE touching either.
